sections.title: Advanced Partnership Concept
sections.content: Level 2 questions may include partners investing for different durations, a new partner joining mid-way, or giving a part of profit as salary/bonus. Profit sharing is always based on (Capital × Time) ratio, but special conditions like salary or bonus are applied first.

sections.title: Time-Based Partnership in ₹
sections.content:
Example: Ajay invests ₹20000 for 12 months, Vijay invests ₹30000 for 8 months.
Ajay: 20000 × 12 = 240000
Vijay: 30000 × 8 = 240000
Ratio = 1:1 → profit shared equally.

sections.title: New Partner Joining
sections.content:
If a third partner joins, calculate only for the months he invested.
Example: Ram ₹10000 (12 months), Shyam ₹20000 (12 months), Mohan ₹15000 (6 months)
Ratio = 10000×12 : 20000×12 : 15000×6 = 120000 : 240000 : 90000 = 4:8:3

sections.title: Salary or Bonus Deduction
sections.content:
If a partner is given fixed salary, deduct it from total profit first, then share remaining profit in ratio.
Example: Total profit ₹50000, Ajay gets ₹5000 salary. Remaining ₹45000 is shared in ratio.

sections.title: Important Formulas
sections.content:
1. Profit ratio = Capital × Time.
2. Individual Profit = (Person's share / Total share) × Remaining Profit.
3. New partner → consider only his investment duration.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
1. Forgetting to deduct salary/bonus.
2. Confusing months and years.
3. Not simplifying the ratio.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Level 2 partnership questions include time variations, new partners, or special payments. Apply special conditions first, then calculate Capital × Time, form the ratio, and divide profit.

tricks.title: Equal Effect Shortcut
tricks.explanation: If Capital × Time is equal, profit is equal.

tricks.title: Convert Time to Months
tricks.explanation: Convert all durations to months to avoid mistakes.

tricks.title: Deduct Salary First
tricks.explanation: Subtract fixed salary from total profit before applying ratio.

tricks.title: Quick Ratio Simplification
tricks.explanation: Divide big numbers by common factor to simplify.

tricks.title: Midway Partner Trick
tricks.explanation: Only consider his invested months for ratio.

tricks.title: One Part Calculation
tricks.explanation: Total Profit ÷ Total parts = value of one part.
tricks.example: ₹84000 profit, ratio 4:3 → total parts 7 → one part ₹12000

tricks.title: Half-Year Profit Shortcut
tricks.explanation: If capital same and time is half, profit is half.

tricks.title: Loss Shares Same as Profit
tricks.explanation: Loss is shared in same ratio as profit.
